passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of different cognitive training programs on reaction time in adults aged 30–50. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four groups: a control group that received no training, and three experimental groups that underwent distinct training protocols (A, B, and C). Each participant performed a computerized Stroop task before and after a four-week training period. The primary outcome was the mean reaction time (in seconds) on incongruent trials. The study aimed to determine which training protocol most effectively reduced reaction time and to assess the magnitude of improvement relative to the control group. The researchers also recorded standard deviations to evaluate variability within each group. The data were analyzed using ANOVA followed by post-hoc comparisons. The results indicated that all training groups showed significant improvements, but the magnitude varied across protocols. These findings have implications for designing targeted interventions to enhance cognitive processing speed in middle-aged adults.
stem: Which group had the lowest mean reaction time after the training period?
explanation: The table shows Treatment B had the lowest mean response time (0.460 s) compared to all other groups.
trap: Choosing Treatment A or the Control group instead of comparing all four means; Treatment B has the lowest mean at 0.46 s.

stem: Which experimental design best controls for potential confounding variables such as baseline cognitive ability?

options.A: All participants receive the same training protocol.
options.B: Random assignment to control and experimental groups.
options.C: Only measuring reaction time after training.
options.D: Using a large sample size without randomization.

explanation: Random assignment distributes confounding variables evenly across groups, reducing bias.
trap: Students may think that giving everyone the same training controls for confounders, but it eliminates the comparison needed.

stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding the data presented?

options.A: Treatment B had the greatest improvement over Control.
options.B: All experimental groups showed significant improvements.
options.C: Standard deviation was smallest in Treatment B.
options.D: Treatment C had the highest mean response time.

explanation: Treatment C’s mean is 0.500 s, which is lower than Control’s 0.520 s, so it does not have the highest mean.
trap: Students may assume that higher mean equals worse performance, but the question asks for the highest numeric mean.

stem: What is the percent reduction in mean reaction time for Treatment B relative to the Control group?
explanation: Correct: (0.52 − 0.46)/0.52 × 100 = 11.5%. Why the others are wrong: B) 13.0% divides by the Treatment B mean (0.46) instead of the Control mean. C) 6.0% is the absolute difference in hundredths of a second, not a percent. D) 88.5% is Treatment B's mean as a percent of Control, not the reduction.
trap: Dividing by the Treatment B mean, or reporting the remaining percentage (88.5%), instead of dividing the reduction by the Control mean.
